text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers.
- The Confederation of Independent Unions, which is divided into two poles, has not yet decided when to hold a congress to elect a new management board.
- Most government ministers have begun their holidays.
- The government is expected to send the 1997 budget proposal, which was adopted last week, to parliament this week.
- The parliamentary board of international relations will hold a hearing of five ambassadorial candidates in September.
- Open-air swimming pools in Slovenia complain of a decline in number of guests due to bad weather this summer.
- A group of archeologists found a tool made from bone between 40,000 to 50,000 years ago in the village of Sebrelje, north of Ljubljana.
- The Ministry of Education will subsidise students' rents in private appartments by 9,000 tolars ($52.5) per month for each student.
- Slovenian health institutions will this year use up about 150 billion tolars from the budget ($0.9 billion).
- The paper cites rumours that Austrian ski jumper Andreas Golberger could decide to jump for the national team of Slovenia after he was suspended from Austria's jumping team.
